explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/679: can one show the stronger version, ω(n−k) < log k/log log k + O(1), is false? DottedCalculator did. The statement is the exact negation of the strong version: for every C and K, all large n have some K < k < n with ω(n−k) ≥ log k/log log k + C. A Lean proof is linked. Faithful.
